bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Execution ramp-up delays impacting FY27 guidance; Government awarding momentum stalling again; Working capital days inflated (132 days) due to revenue denominator effect; Debt reduction slower than peers due to strategic asset retention.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident on order book quality and diversification; Candid on execution lull impacting current metrics; Defensive on debt levels (framed as strategic choice to hold assets); Optimistic on FY27 inflection.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Management explicitly frames the 'elevated' debt as a strategic choice to hold annuity assets (InvIT units) rather than a liquidity crisis; if they had sold these assets, net debt would be ~INR400-500 Cr; they are effectively levered long on their own infrastructure assets.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Stated 'Way Ahead' capital philosophy: transfer matured roads, power, renewable and transmission assets to InvITs, increase the share of recurring distribution income, drive capital recycling into new growth opportunities and 'Accelerate Parent Consolidated balance sheet deleveraging'.
- Explicit target: 'To be Net Debt positive on Standalone levels'; EPC strategy is 'scale-driven growth with margin-led, selective bidding' and MDO strategy is to establish mining as a core earnings engine by ramping production at existing assets.
- Balance sheet as on Jun'26: net debt Rs 2,106 Cr against equity of Rs 6,873 Cr, with net debt to equity rising from 0.28 as on Mar'26 to 0.31 as on Jun'26 (split into working capital debt/equity 0.27 and equipment debt/equity 0.04).
- Working capital days increased from 131 days as on Mar'26 to 133 days as on Jun'26.
- Asset monetisation record: of 33 completed HAM projects, 19 are fully divested (16 to Shrem Group/Shrem InvIT and 3 to Cube Highways) and of the remaining 14, seven were 100% divested to Anantam Highways InvIT, four will be divested 100%/49% to Anantam Highways InvIT in Aug-26 and three will be 100% divested to InvIT in June-27; of 6 under-construction HAM projects, 4 have 24.99% divested to Alpha Alternative and 2 remain 100% DBL-held.
- MDO uses a separate SPV per project with ring-fenced assets, liabilities and cash flows, giving 'transparent monitoring and monetisation flexibility'.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- In-house end-to-end execution across 11 sectors — design, engineering, procurement, construction, equipment deployment, material production and site monitoring — with 100% of projects executed using own teams and equipment, shortening decision cycles and giving greater control over cost and schedule.
- One of India's largest owned construction equipment fleets, with 10,275+ units spanning excavators, cranes, pavers, crushers, concrete plants and mining trucks, allowing rapid mobilisation, simultaneous multi-site support and reduced dependence on external equipment hire when industry demand is high.
- Backward integration through three in-house manufacturing units and an in-house foundry producing crash barriers, signage, poles, gantries, bearings, reinforced earth walls and cast components, giving control over material quality, cost and delivery schedules.
- Execution track record: around 90% of projects are completed ahead of schedule, with a cumulative early completion bonus of Rs 580 Cr received across several road contracts, and early delivery enabling redeployment of equipment and teams.
- Long-tenure contracted MDO franchise — coal and bauxite contracts with secured tenures of 25 to 55 years with Punjab State Power Corporation, Mahanadi Coalfields and National Aluminium Company — providing a volume-linked revenue model with earnings visibility and predictable cash flows.
- Diversified multi-vertical order book of Rs 28,830 Cr spread across mining, roads, renewables, irrigation, transmission, tunnels, bridges, metro, optical fibre and water, reducing dependence on any single vertical.
- Pan-India presence across 20 states and 1 Union Territory, built up over 35+ years of operation.
- Capital-recycling capability demonstrated by the 2017 sale of a 24-asset road portfolio with an economic value of Rs 10,500 Cr, the FY25 divestment of road HAM assets to Alpha Alternatives, and the October 2025 listing of Anantam Highways InvIT.
- Site technology stack — drones for progress monitoring and volumetric surveys, GPS, fuel telematics and digital dashboards, with fleet telematics delivering roughly 25% fuel saving, and surface miners in mining operations reducing the need for drilling and blasting.
- SAP HANA ERP providing an integrated business operations platform across all functions with embedded checks and controls.
- Government and PSU counterparties described as having strong credit worthiness, limiting credit risk on trade receivables.
- In-house quality control with on-site laboratories and dedicated quality teams testing materials and work against client specifications at each stage of execution.
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Commodity price risk on core construction inputs — The Company is exposed to price fluctuations in bitumen, cement, steel and crushed stone required for road projects; mitigated through forward booking, inventory management, vendor development and price-escalation clauses in client contracts. Toward the close of FY26, geopolitical tensions in West Asia raised global crude prices, translating into elevated bitumen, diesel and freight costs across the construction value chain.
- Concentration on government and PSU counterparties — BRSR states the clientele consists of the Central Government, State Governments, government agencies and public sector enterprises; credit risk is described as limited because customers are mainly government-promoted entities, but it leaves receivables and order inflow dependent on public capital-expenditure cycles and award timing.
- Single-activity, single-country concentration — BRSR reports construction (roads, highways, railways, mining and utility projects) as 100% of turnover with no international operations and exports not applicable, so there is no diversification outside Indian infrastructure construction.
- Interest rate and market risk on a leveraged balance sheet — Market risk affects borrowings, trade and other payables, security deposits, receivables and bank deposits; the Company states its activities are exposed to interest rate risk and manages it through a mix of fund-raising and investment products across maturity profiles.
- Liquidity risk — The Company may be unable to meet present and future cash flow and collateral obligations without incurring unacceptable losses; it monitors liquidity levels and capital market conditions and maintains access to banking lines, trade finance and capital markets.
- Credit risk on trade receivables and unbilled work-in-progress — Assessed via a provision matrix using external and internal credit factors, credit ratings, financial condition, receivable ageing and historical experience — reflecting the working-capital intensity of EPC execution.
- Regulatory and compliance risk — The Company is exposed to risks attached to various statutes, laws and regulations, mitigated through regular review of legal compliances via internal control and audits.
- Human resource risk — Retaining existing talent and attracting new talent are described as major risks; countered with training, learning and development integration and employee schemes for drivers and machine operators.
- Project-award and execution-timing risk — Management notes road project awards remained relatively subdued for much of FY26 on account of land acquisition timelines, state election cycles and administrative recalibration, and that competitive intensity from undercapitalised players distorted the market.

business.body:
- Described as a 'Pan-India listed infrastructure company combining Execution, Asset Ownership and Annuity Cash Flows' with 35+ years in infrastructure development, presence across 20 States and 1 Union Territory, 21,221+ employees and a 10,394+ equipment fleet; deck claims ~90% early completion.
- The DBL 2.0 structure is framed as three engines: EPC as the 'Execution Engine' and capability backbone across 12 sectors, MDO as the 'Long-Term Cash Flow Engine' with secured 25-55 year tenure and volume-linked revenue, and the Multi Asset Platform / InvIT as the 'Value Unlocking Engine' converting built assets into income-generating financial assets.
- Integrated model is summarised as 'EPC BUILDS. ASSETS DELIVER. CASH FLOWS SUSTAIN.' — EPC margins are earned by DBL, MDO and PPP InvIT assets generate long-duration cash flows, and cash generated from assets is upstreamed and reinvested into DBL.
- Established pan-India developer: over the last two decades (FY2006-07 to FY2025-26) total revenue of Rs 98,872 Cr, of which home state Rs 9,731 Cr (9.84%) and rest of India Rs 89,141 Cr (90.16%).
- History spans four phases from a 1987 proprietorship in real estate construction, through first road project in 2001, a 22x-oversubscribed IPO in 2016, the 2017 sale of 24 road assets at ~Rs 10,500 Cr enterprise value, to net worth crossing Rs 5,000 Cr in 2024 and the 2025 listing of Anantam Highways InvIT.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [InvIT platform] Anantam Highways Trust is an Indian infrastructure investment trust sponsored by Alpha Alternatives Fund Advisors LLP, whose initial portfolio comprises seven national highway projects in Karnataka, Telangana, Gujarat, Bihar, Tamil Nadu and the union territory of Puducherry, to be acquired via 100% shareholding in seven Project SPVs (DBHL, DHHL, RHL, VHL, NPHL, BMHL and MBHL).
- [InvIT platform] Shrem InvIT holds projects located in Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Uttar Pradesh, Gujarat and Karnataka; upcoming assets earmarked for InvIT transfer span roads, transmission, renewable and oil and gas.
- [Order book contradiction] The Company Overview slide states a 'Rs 30,215 Cr Diversified Order Book across 12 verticals', while the order book slide states 'Order Book as at 30th June 2026 of Rs. 27,691 Cr' with a footnote that it 'Excludes: New Irrigation Project won in July 2026 in the state of Chhattisgarh, with a total project cost of Rs. 2,524.32 Cr' — both readings are quoted here without reconciliation.
- [Mining order book treatment] The company holds long-term order book from its Mining MDOs for the next 25-55 years but has included only 3 years of rolling orders worth Rs 5,224 Cr in the reported order book (Rs 2,247 Cr from DBL Siarmal Coal Mines, Rs 1,374 Cr from Pachhwara Coal Mine and Rs 1,603 Cr from DBL Pottangi Bauxite Mines).
- [Leadership] Dilip Suryavanshi is Chairman and Managing Director (43+ years in construction, President of the Madhya Pradesh Builders Association) and Devendra Jain is Managing Director and CEO (26+ years); the senior team includes Rohan Suryavanshi (Head – Strategy & Planning), Karan Suryavanshi (Head – Business Development), Bharat Singh (President) and Sanjay Bansal (CFO, joined 2022).
business.title: Notable from the deck

business.body: The Company designs, procures and constructs infrastructure across eleven sectors — roads and highways, irrigation, water supply, tunnels, metros and railways, special bridges and urban development, mining, renewable energy, power transmission, optical fibre cabling and petroleum pipelines — executing projects through the full design, procurement and construction cycle with its own teams and equipment. Its customers are the Central Government, State Governments, government agencies and public sector enterprises, including the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways, the National Highways Authority of India, the Airports Authority of India and Coal India Limited and its subsidiaries; construction accounted for 100% of turnover in FY26 and all operations are within India. Alongside EPC, it operates coal and bauxite mines as a Mine Developer and Operator under 25 to 55 year contracts and recycles mature road assets into the Anantam Highways InvIT.

outlook.body:
- DBL 2.0: evolve from project-by-project EPC execution into a platform that builds, operates and owns infrastructure assets, run as three engines — EPC (execution), MDO (long-term cash flow) and a multi-asset InvIT platform (value unlocking).
- Margin-led, selective bidding: pursue growth by choosing projects with clear margin visibility, balanced risk and reward and strong counterparties, rather than chasing volume; management describes the FY26 revenue moderation as a conscious outcome of this discipline.
- Shift the mix toward asset-light, high-ROIC segments — water, urban infrastructure, renewables and power transmission — which use less capital and lift return on investment.
- Broaden the EPC platform across more sectors to give steadier revenue visibility and improve capital efficiency across market cycles.
- Ramp up production at the existing Siarmal and Pachhwara mines toward contracted capacity and capture operating leverage as volumes rise.
- Widen the MDO franchise beyond coal and beyond India — add new mine-development mandates in India and overseas and broaden the mineral base, as with the Pottangi bauxite MDO contract.
- Establish mining as a core, recurring earnings engine and a primary source of group profit and cash flow.
- Transfer matured assets into InvITs: move the remaining 11 road assets into Anantam Highways InvIT in a phased manner, with power, renewable and transmission assets to follow as they mature.
- Hold InvIT units for predictable long-term distribution income and recycle freed-up equity into fresh projects across roads, transmission, renewables and other asset classes.
- Keep the standalone balance sheet light through capital recycling and capital discipline, and accelerate consolidated deleveraging using asset transfers and structured equity to lower financing cost.
- Embed sustainability through the Geo Green initiative, rooftop solar at the Bhopal and Indore facilities, responsible resource management and road-safety and community programmes.

outlook.body: DBL's expansion in FY26 was driven by order wins and new special-purpose vehicles rather than by manufacturing capacity additions. The Company secured 13 new projects worth Rs 18,548 Cr across 8 states, its highest-ever annual order intake, spanning HAM, EPC, MDO, renewable energy and power transmission, and completed five projects during the year. Named new mandates include a Rs 4,900 Cr Feeder Solarization programme under PM KUSUM-C in Madhya Pradesh (its largest-ever renewable energy order), a Rs 3,400 Cr Ganga Path connecting Sultanganj-Bhagalpur-Sabour Road in Bihar, a Rs 2,034 Cr Bandh Baretha hybrid annuity feeder project in Rajasthan (its maiden water HAM entry), a Rs 1,850 Cr 400 kV sub-station at Mekhali with associated transmission lines in Karnataka (its maiden power transmission entry), a Rs 1,750 Cr MDO contract for the development and operation of the Pottangi bauxite mines with an overland conveyor corridor in Odisha (extending the mining franchise beyond coal), a Rs 1,277 Cr metro viaduct and 14 elevated stations in Haryana, a Rs 1,115 Cr industrial corridor at the Palakkad node in Kerala, a Rs 698 Cr flood-protection embankment on the Narmada in Gujarat, a Rs 279 Cr 100 MW grid-connected ground-mounted captive solar PV project in Madhya Pradesh, and a Rs 124 Cr ATF pipeline from Navgam to Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel International Airport in Gujarat. In mining, the operating portfolio comprises the Siarmal and Pachhwara coal mines, where FY26 production reached 28.72 million metric tonnes against the annual production target, with coal production targeted to reach approximately 57 million metric tonnes annually by FY29 and volumes to be lifted toward contracted capacity. The Company incorporated 16 new SPVs during and shortly after the year, including DBL ERCP Bandh Baretha (Nov 2025), DBL Paramakudi-Ramanathapuram Highways (Dec 2025), DBL Pottangi Bauxite Mines (Dec 2025), nine district-level solar companies in Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan (Dhar, Sukheda Ratlam, Guna, Vidisha, Rajgarh, Shajapur, Bhopal and Mandsaur, Dec 2025-Jan 2026), DBL Renewable (Jan 2026), DBL Power Transmission Project (Jan 2026), DBL Solar Energy (Feb 2026), DBL Ahmedabad ATF Pipeline (Mar 2026) and GreenION Energy Solutions (Apr 2026). Renewable-energy activity includes over 1,363 MW of grid-connected solar capacity under EPC execution and a 100 MW captive solar project under development, alongside rooftop solar installations at the Bhopal and Indore facilities. Supporting infrastructure includes three in-house manufacturing units producing crash barriers, signage, poles, gantries, bearings, reinforced earth walls and cast components with an in-house foundry, and an owned fleet of over 10,275 equipment units. On the asset side, expansion is paired with recycling: the Anantam Highways InvIT was listed in October 2025, seven road SPVs were transferred into it, and the remaining 11 road assets are to be moved into the trust in a phased manner with power, renewable and transmission assets to follow as they mature.

outlook.body:
- Sustained public investment in infrastructure and a long-term policy commitment to nation building, anchored by the Union Budget's record Rs 12.22 lakh crore capital outlay for FY 2026-27 and a robust public-private partnership pipeline.
- India continues to be the world's fastest-growing major economy, and management sees the outlook for Indian infrastructure as compelling, supported by an expanding project pipeline and deepening asset-monetisation markets.
- Execution momentum varied by segment: road project awards remained relatively subdued for much of the year on account of land-acquisition timelines, state election cycles and administrative recalibration, while water, metro, railways, mining and renewable energy continued to attract encouraging investment activity.
- Earnings-quality mix shift: the increasing contribution from the coal MDO business, together with gains recognised on the transfer of HAM assets to Anantam Highways InvIT, strengthened the quality and sustainability of consolidated earnings.
- MDO contracts with Punjab State Power Corporation Limited, Mahanadi Coalfields Limited and National Aluminium Company Limited carry 25 to 55 year tenures and a volume-linked revenue model, giving contracted revenue visibility and predictable cash flows.
- Recurring distribution income from investments in Anantam Highways InvIT and Shrem InvIT builds a stable income stream and supports the deleveraging strategy.
- Cost headwind: the escalation of geopolitical tensions in West Asia toward the close of the fiscal year raised global crude prices, translating into elevated bitumen, diesel and freight costs across the construction value chain.
- Competitive intensity from undercapitalised players distorted the market over the previous two award cycles, which management responded to by preserving threshold margins rather than pursuing volume.
- Backward integration, an owned fleet of 10,275+ equipment units and in-house execution across 11 sectors support margin protection and schedule control.
- Year-end order book stood at Rs 28,830 Crore, an all-time high and described as well diversified across the multi-vertical infrastructure platform.
- Total order inflows for FY26 reached Rs 18,548 Crore, the highest in the Company's history, comfortably exceeding management's guidance for the year.
- The Company secured 13 new project wins spanning HAM, EPC, MDO, renewable energy and power transmission segments across 8 states.
- Order-book vertical mix: Mining Rs 5,832 Crore (20%), Roads and Highways Rs 5,425 Crore (19%), Renewable Energy Rs 5,179 Crore (18%), Irrigation Rs 4,651 Crore (16%), Power Transmission Rs 1,850 Crore (6%), Tunnels Rs 1,689 Crore (6%), Special Bridges and Urban Development Rs 1,646 Crore (6%), Metro and Railways Rs 1,275 Crore (4%), Optical Fibre Rs 788 Crore (3%), Water Supply Rs 371 Crore (1%) and Petroleum and Gas Rs 124 Crore.
- The mining line in the order book reflects only 3 years of rolling orders worth Rs 5,146 Crore from the mining MDOs (Rs 2,161 Crore from DBL Siarmal, Rs 1,352 Crore from Pachhwara and Rs 1,633 Crore from DBL Pottangi), even though the underlying MDO order book runs for the next 25 to 55 years.
- Largest FY26 wins include a Rs 4,900 Crore Feeder Solarization mandate under PM KUSUM-C in Madhya Pradesh (the largest-ever renewable energy order), a Rs 3,400 Crore Ganga Path project in Bihar, a Rs 2,034 Crore Bandh Baretha hybrid annuity water project in Rajasthan, a Rs 1,850 Crore 400 kV sub-station and transmission project in Karnataka and a Rs 1,750 Crore Pottangi bauxite mines MDO contract in Odisha.
- The Bandh Baretha and Karnataka transmission wins mark the Company's maiden entries into water hybrid annuity and power transmission respectively; the Pottangi contract extends the mining franchise beyond coal.
- The order book has grown from Rs 14,923 Crore in FY22 to Rs 17,432 Crore in FY23, Rs 25,595 Crore in FY24, Rs 25,395 Crore in FY25 and Rs 28,830 Crore in FY26.
- Geographically the order book spans states including Madhya Pradesh (19.43%), Odisha (16.91%), Bihar (11.79%), Rajasthan (8.40%), Jharkhand (8.27%), Kerala (7.34%), Karnataka (7.21%) and Gujarat (5.53%).

currentContext.strategies: DBL 2.0: evolve from project-by-project EPC execution into a platform that builds, operates and owns infrastructure assets, run as three engines — EPC (execution), MDO (long-term cash flow) and a multi-asset InvIT platform (value unlocking).|Margin-led, selective bidding: pursue growth by choosing projects with clear margin visibility, balanced risk and reward and strong counterparties, rather than chasing volume; management describes the FY26 revenue moderation as a conscious outcome of this discipline.|Shift the mix toward asset-light, high-ROIC segments — water, urban infrastructure, renewables and power transmission — which use less capital and lift return on investment.|Broaden the EPC platform across more sectors to give steadier revenue visibility and improve capital efficiency across market cycles.|Ramp up production at the existing Siarmal and Pachhwara mines toward contracted capacity and capture operating leverage as volumes rise.|Widen the MDO franchise beyond coal and beyond India — add new mine-development mandates in India and overseas and broaden the mineral base, as with the Pottangi bauxite MDO contract.|Establish mining as a core, recurring earnings engine and a primary source of group profit and cash flow.|Transfer matured assets into InvITs: move the remaining 11 road assets into Anantam Highways InvIT in a phased manner, with power, renewable and transmission assets to follow as they mature.|Hold InvIT units for predictable long-term distribution income and recycle freed-up equity into fresh projects across roads, transmission, renewables and other asset classes.|Keep the standalone balance sheet light through capital recycling and capital discipline, and accelerate consolidated deleveraging using asset transfers and structured equity to lower financing cost.|Embed sustainability through the Geo Green initiative, rooftop solar at the Bhopal and Indore facilities, responsible resource management and road-safety and community programmes.
currentContext.expansion: DBL's expansion in FY26 was driven by order wins and new special-purpose vehicles rather than by manufacturing capacity additions. The Company secured 13 new projects worth Rs 18,548 Cr across 8 states, its highest-ever annual order intake, spanning HAM, EPC, MDO, renewable energy and power transmission, and completed five projects during the year. Named new mandates include a Rs 4,900 Cr Feeder Solarization programme under PM KUSUM-C in Madhya Pradesh (its largest-ever renewable energy order), a Rs 3,400 Cr Ganga Path connecting Sultanganj-Bhagalpur-Sabour Road in Bihar, a Rs 2,034 Cr Bandh Baretha hybrid annuity feeder project in Rajasthan (its maiden water HAM entry), a Rs 1,850 Cr 400 kV sub-station at Mekhali with associated transmission lines in Karnataka (its maiden power transmission entry), a Rs 1,750 Cr MDO contract for the development and operation of the Pottangi bauxite mines with an overland conveyor corridor in Odisha (extending the mining franchise beyond coal), a Rs 1,277 Cr metro viaduct and 14 elevated stations in Haryana, a Rs 1,115 Cr industrial corridor at the Palakkad node in Kerala, a Rs 698 Cr flood-protection embankment on the Narmada in Gujarat, a Rs 279 Cr 100 MW grid-connected ground-mounted captive solar PV project in Madhya Pradesh, and a Rs 124 Cr ATF pipeline from Navgam to Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel International Airport in Gujarat. In mining, the operating portfolio comprises the Siarmal and Pachhwara coal mines, where FY26 production reached 28.72 million metric tonnes against the annual production target, with coal production targeted to reach approximately 57 million metric tonnes annually by FY29 and volumes to be lifted toward contracted capacity. The Company incorporated 16 new SPVs during and shortly after the year, including DBL ERCP Bandh Baretha (Nov 2025), DBL Paramakudi-Ramanathapuram Highways (Dec 2025), DBL Pottangi Bauxite Mines (Dec 2025), nine district-level solar companies in Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan (Dhar, Sukheda Ratlam, Guna, Vidisha, Rajgarh, Shajapur, Bhopal and Mandsaur, Dec 2025-Jan 2026), DBL Renewable (Jan 2026), DBL Power Transmission Project (Jan 2026), DBL Solar Energy (Feb 2026), DBL Ahmedabad ATF Pipeline (Mar 2026) and GreenION Energy Solutions (Apr 2026). Renewable-energy activity includes over 1,363 MW of grid-connected solar capacity under EPC execution and a 100 MW captive solar project under development, alongside rooftop solar installations at the Bhopal and Indore facilities. Supporting infrastructure includes three in-house manufacturing units producing crash barriers, signage, poles, gantries, bearings, reinforced earth walls and cast components with an in-house foundry, and an owned fleet of over 10,275 equipment units. On the asset side, expansion is paired with recycling: the Anantam Highways InvIT was listed in October 2025, seven road SPVs were transferred into it, and the remaining 11 road assets are to be moved into the trust in a phased manner with power, renewable and transmission assets to follow as they mature.

risks.risk: Commodity price risk on core construction inputs
risks.note: The Company is exposed to price fluctuations in bitumen, cement, steel and crushed stone required for road projects; mitigated through forward booking, inventory management, vendor development and price-escalation clauses in client contracts. Toward the close of FY26, geopolitical tensions in West Asia raised global crude prices, translating into elevated bitumen, diesel and freight costs across the construction value chain.

one-line thesis: DBL secured a historic INR17,900 Cr order inflow (diversified beyond roads) creating a ~INR29,300 Cr book, yet Q3 revenue fell 23% YoY due to prior execution lulls; profitability surged on a one-off INR577 Cr InvIT flip gain, masking core EPC margin compression, while management guides for a 30-40% revenue rebound in FY27 driven by new awards and mining scale-up.
financial scorecard: Revenue (9M): INR6,684 Cr (-19% YoY); EBITDA (9M): INR1,373 Cr (-8% YoY, margin ~20.5%); PAT (9M): INR1,275 Cr (+126% YoY, boosted by INR577 Cr exceptional InvIT gain); Order Book: INR29,300 Cr (record high); Net Debt: ~INR2,100 Cr (flat QoQ, elevated due to muted execution vs. asset retention strategy). One-offs: INR577 Cr pre-tax gain from flipping 7 assets to Anantam InvIT (tax-exempt under Sec 47(17)).
guidance: Revenue Growth: FY26 closing ~INR7,000-7,500 Cr; FY27 guidance ~INR10,000 Cr (+30-40% YoY); Margin: FY27 EBITDA margin target 12-13% (up from ~10.4%); Order Inflow: FY27 target INR10,000-15,000 Cr; Capex: Parent level capped at ~INR100 Cr (replacement only); SPV-level capex funded via project debt.

growth verticals / optionality: Coal MDO scaling to 57 MT by FY29 (8-9% of India's output); Water HAM and Urban Infra pipeline expanding; Renewable platform (Solar/Transmission) with structured equity partners limiting parent capital outlay; Potential demerger/listing of mining arm long-term.
margins & cost dynamics: Q3 margins pressured by low operating leverage; FY27 margin recovery to 12-13% expected as execution normalizes; structural cost rationalization achieved (headcount halved to 19k vs peak 38k); SPV-level mining EBITDA margins in mid-teens.
capex / expansion: Parent capex moderated to ~INR100 Cr/year (down from INR500 Cr peak); Major growth capex behind us; Future SPV capex (Solar/Transmission/Coal) funded at project level via debt/mezzanine, not parent balance sheet.
capital allocation: Strategy shifted to 'DBL 2.0': Retain assets in InvITs for annuity income rather than immediate debt paydown; Targeting net debt free by FY28; Plan to reduce debt by INR700-800 Cr in FY27; Holding INR1,600 Cr in InvIT units (Anantam/Shrem) + ~INR500 Cr cash in Coal SPVs.
risks & watch-items: Execution ramp-up delays impacting FY27 guidance; Government awarding momentum stalling again; Working capital days inflated (132 days) due to revenue denominator effect; Debt reduction slower than peers due to strategic asset retention.
management quality / tone: Confident on order book quality and diversification; Candid on execution lull impacting current metrics; Defensive on debt levels (framed as strategic choice to hold assets); Optimistic on FY27 inflection.
non-obvious takeaways: Management explicitly frames the 'elevated' debt as a strategic choice to hold annuity assets (InvIT units) rather than a liquidity crisis; if they had sold these assets, net debt would be ~INR400-500 Cr; they are effectively levered long on their own infrastructure assets.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Dilip Buildcon is a pan-India diversified infrastructure company that has grown over 35+ years from a road-focused EPC contractor into a three-engine platform combining EPC execution, long-tenure coal and bauxite mine development and operation, and an InvIT-based asset-monetisation business.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: The Company designs, procures and constructs infrastructure across eleven sectors — roads and highways, irrigation, water supply, tunnels, metros and railways, special bridges and urban development, mining, renewable energy, power transmission, optical fibre cabling and petroleum pipelines — executing projects through the full design, procurement and construction cycle with its own teams and equipment. Its customers are the Central Government, State Governments, government agencies and public sector enterprises, including the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways, the National Highways Authority of India, the Airports Authority of India and Coal India Limited and its subsidiaries; construction accounted for 100% of turnover in FY26 and all operations are within India. Alongside EPC, it operates coal and bauxite mines as a Mine Developer and Operator under 25 to 55 year contracts and recycles mature road assets into the Anantam Highways InvIT.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Sustained public investment in infrastructure and a long-term policy commitment to nation building, anchored by the Union Budget's record Rs 12.22 lakh crore capital outlay for FY 2026-27 and a robust public-private partnership pipeline.
- India continues to be the world's fastest-growing major economy, and management sees the outlook for Indian infrastructure as compelling, supported by an expanding project pipeline and deepening asset-monetisation markets.
- Execution momentum varied by segment: road project awards remained relatively subdued for much of the year on account of land-acquisition timelines, state election cycles and administrative recalibration, while water, metro, railways, mining and renewable energy continued to attract encouraging investment activity.
- Earnings-quality mix shift: the increasing contribution from the coal MDO business, together with gains recognised on the transfer of HAM assets to Anantam Highways InvIT, strengthened the quality and sustainability of consolidated earnings.
- MDO contracts with Punjab State Power Corporation Limited, Mahanadi Coalfields Limited and National Aluminium Company Limited carry 25 to 55 year tenures and a volume-linked revenue model, giving contracted revenue visibility and predictable cash flows.
- Recurring distribution income from investments in Anantam Highways InvIT and Shrem InvIT builds a stable income stream and supports the deleveraging strategy.
- Cost headwind: the escalation of geopolitical tensions in West Asia toward the close of the fiscal year raised global crude prices, translating into elevated bitumen, diesel and freight costs across the construction value chain.
- Competitive intensity from undercapitalised players distorted the market over the previous two award cycles, which management responded to by preserving threshold margins rather than pursuing volume.
- Backward integration, an owned fleet of 10,275+ equipment units and in-house execution across 11 sectors support margin protection and schedule control.
- Year-end order book stood at Rs 28,830 Crore, an all-time high and described as well diversified across the multi-vertical infrastructure platform.
- Total order inflows for FY26 reached Rs 18,548 Crore, the highest in the Company's history, comfortably exceeding management's guidance for the year.
- The Company secured 13 new project wins spanning HAM, EPC, MDO, renewable energy and power transmission segments across 8 states.
- Order-book vertical mix: Mining Rs 5,832 Crore (20%), Roads and Highways Rs 5,425 Crore (19%), Renewable Energy Rs 5,179 Crore (18%), Irrigation Rs 4,651 Crore (16%), Power Transmission Rs 1,850 Crore (6%), Tunnels Rs 1,689 Crore (6%), Special Bridges and Urban Development Rs 1,646 Crore (6%), Metro and Railways Rs 1,275 Crore (4%), Optical Fibre Rs 788 Crore (3%), Water Supply Rs 371 Crore (1%) and Petroleum and Gas Rs 124 Crore.
- The mining line in the order book reflects only 3 years of rolling orders worth Rs 5,146 Crore from the mining MDOs (Rs 2,161 Crore from DBL Siarmal, Rs 1,352 Crore from Pachhwara and Rs 1,633 Crore from DBL Pottangi), even though the underlying MDO order book runs for the next 25 to 55 years.
- Largest FY26 wins include a Rs 4,900 Crore Feeder Solarization mandate under PM KUSUM-C in Madhya Pradesh (the largest-ever renewable energy order), a Rs 3,400 Crore Ganga Path project in Bihar, a Rs 2,034 Crore Bandh Baretha hybrid annuity water project in Rajasthan, a Rs 1,850 Crore 400 kV sub-station and transmission project in Karnataka and a Rs 1,750 Crore Pottangi bauxite mines MDO contract in Odisha.
- The Bandh Baretha and Karnataka transmission wins mark the Company's maiden entries into water hybrid annuity and power transmission respectively; the Pottangi contract extends the mining franchise beyond coal.
- The order book has grown from Rs 14,923 Crore in FY22 to Rs 17,432 Crore in FY23, Rs 25,595 Crore in FY24, Rs 25,395 Crore in FY25 and Rs 28,830 Crore in FY26.
- Geographically the order book spans states including Madhya Pradesh (19.43%), Odisha (16.91%), Bihar (11.79%), Rajasthan (8.40%), Jharkhand (8.27%), Kerala (7.34%), Karnataka (7.21%) and Gujarat (5.53%).

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: Q3 margins pressured by low operating leverage; FY27 margin recovery to 12-13% expected as execution normalizes; structural cost rationalization achieved (headcount halved to 19k vs peak 38k); SPV-level mining EBITDA margins in mid-teens.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Strategy shifted to 'DBL 2.0': Retain assets in InvITs for annuity income rather than immediate debt paydown; Targeting net debt free by FY28; Plan to reduce debt by INR700-800 Cr in FY27; Holding INR1,600 Cr in InvIT units (Anantam/Shrem) + ~INR500 Cr cash in Coal SPVs.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: DBL's expansion in FY26 was driven by order wins and new special-purpose vehicles rather than by manufacturing capacity additions. The Company secured 13 new projects worth Rs 18,548 Cr across 8 states, its highest-ever annual order intake, spanning HAM, EPC, MDO, renewable energy and power transmission, and completed five projects during the year. Named new mandates include a Rs 4,900 Cr Feeder Solarization programme under PM KUSUM-C in Madhya Pradesh (its largest-ever renewable energy order), a Rs 3,400 Cr Ganga Path connecting Sultanganj-Bhagalpur-Sabour Road in Bihar, a Rs 2,034 Cr Bandh Baretha hybrid annuity feeder project in Rajasthan (its maiden water HAM entry), a Rs 1,850 Cr 400 kV sub-station at Mekhali with associated transmission lines in Karnataka (its maiden power transmission entry), a Rs 1,750 Cr MDO contract for the development and operation of the Pottangi bauxite mines with an overland conveyor corridor in Odisha (extending the mining franchise beyond coal), a Rs 1,277 Cr metro viaduct and 14 elevated stations in Haryana, a Rs 1,115 Cr industrial corridor at the Palakkad node in Kerala, a Rs 698 Cr flood-protection embankment on the Narmada in Gujarat, a Rs 279 Cr 100 MW grid-connected ground-mounted captive solar PV project in Madhya Pradesh, and a Rs 124 Cr ATF pipeline from Navgam to Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel International Airport in Gujarat. In mining, the operating portfolio comprises the Siarmal and Pachhwara coal mines, where FY26 production reached 28.72 million metric tonnes against the annual production target, with coal production targeted to reach approximately 57 million metric tonnes annually by FY29 and volumes to be lifted toward contracted capacity. The Company incorporated 16 new SPVs during and shortly after the year, including DBL ERCP Bandh Baretha (Nov 2025), DBL Paramakudi-Ramanathapuram Highways (Dec 2025), DBL Pottangi Bauxite Mines (Dec 2025), nine district-level solar companies in Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan (Dhar, Sukheda Ratlam, Guna, Vidisha, Rajgarh, Shajapur, Bhopal and Mandsaur, Dec 2025-Jan 2026), DBL Renewable (Jan 2026), DBL Power Transmission Project (Jan 2026), DBL Solar Energy (Feb 2026), DBL Ahmedabad ATF Pipeline (Mar 2026) and GreenION Energy Solutions (Apr 2026). Renewable-energy activity includes over 1,363 MW of grid-connected solar capacity under EPC execution and a 100 MW captive solar project under development, alongside rooftop solar installations at the Bhopal and Indore facilities. Supporting infrastructure includes three in-house manufacturing units producing crash barriers, signage, poles, gantries, bearings, reinforced earth walls and cast components with an in-house foundry, and an owned fleet of over 10,275 equipment units. On the asset side, expansion is paired with recycling: the Anantam Highways InvIT was listed in October 2025, seven road SPVs were transferred into it, and the remaining 11 road assets are to be moved into the trust in a phased manner with power, renewable and transmission assets to follow as they mature.

management_tone.body: Confident on order book quality and diversification; Candid on execution lull impacting current metrics; Defensive on debt levels (framed as strategic choice to hold assets); Optimistic on FY27 inflection.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- In-house end-to-end execution across 11 sectors — design, engineering, procurement, construction, equipment deployment, material production and site monitoring — with 100% of projects executed using own teams and equipment, shortening decision cycles and giving greater control over cost and schedule.
- One of India's largest owned construction equipment fleets, with 10,275+ units spanning excavators, cranes, pavers, crushers, concrete plants and mining trucks, allowing rapid mobilisation, simultaneous multi-site support and reduced dependence on external equipment hire when industry demand is high.
- Backward integration through three in-house manufacturing units and an in-house foundry producing crash barriers, signage, poles, gantries, bearings, reinforced earth walls and cast components, giving control over material quality, cost and delivery schedules.
- Execution track record: around 90% of projects are completed ahead of schedule, with a cumulative early completion bonus of Rs 580 Cr received across several road contracts, and early delivery enabling redeployment of equipment and teams.
- Long-tenure contracted MDO franchise — coal and bauxite contracts with secured tenures of 25 to 55 years with Punjab State Power Corporation, Mahanadi Coalfields and National Aluminium Company — providing a volume-linked revenue model with earnings visibility and predictable cash flows.
- Diversified multi-vertical order book of Rs 28,830 Cr spread across mining, roads, renewables, irrigation, transmission, tunnels, bridges, metro, optical fibre and water, reducing dependence on any single vertical.
- Pan-India presence across 20 states and 1 Union Territory, built up over 35+ years of operation.
- Capital-recycling capability demonstrated by the 2017 sale of a 24-asset road portfolio with an economic value of Rs 10,500 Cr, the FY25 divestment of road HAM assets to Alpha Alternatives, and the October 2025 listing of Anantam Highways InvIT.
- Site technology stack — drones for progress monitoring and volumetric surveys, GPS, fuel telematics and digital dashboards, with fleet telematics delivering roughly 25% fuel saving, and surface miners in mining operations reducing the need for drilling and blasting.
- SAP HANA ERP providing an integrated business operations platform across all functions with embedded checks and controls.
- Government and PSU counterparties described as having strong credit worthiness, limiting credit risk on trade receivables.
- In-house quality control with on-site laboratories and dedicated quality teams testing materials and work against client specifications at each stage of execution.

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Execution ramp-up delays impacting FY27 guidance; Government awarding momentum stalling again; Working capital days inflated (132 days) due to revenue denominator effect; Debt reduction slower than peers due to strategic asset retention.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: Management explicitly frames the 'elevated' debt as a strategic choice to hold annuity assets (InvIT units) rather than a liquidity crisis; if they had sold these assets, net debt would be ~INR400-500 Cr; they are effectively levered long on their own infrastructure assets.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- DBL 2.0: evolve from project-by-project EPC execution into a platform that builds, operates and owns infrastructure assets, run as three engines — EPC (execution), MDO (long-term cash flow) and a multi-asset InvIT platform (value unlocking).
- Margin-led, selective bidding: pursue growth by choosing projects with clear margin visibility, balanced risk and reward and strong counterparties, rather than chasing volume; management describes the FY26 revenue moderation as a conscious outcome of this discipline.
- Shift the mix toward asset-light, high-ROIC segments — water, urban infrastructure, …

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [InvIT platform] Anantam Highways Trust is an Indian infrastructure investment trust sponsored by Alpha Alternatives Fund Advisors LLP, whose initial portfolio comprises seven national highway projects in Karnataka, Telangana, Gujarat, Bihar, Tamil Nadu and the union territory of Puducherry, to be acquired via 100% shareholding in seven Project SPVs (DBHL, DHHL, RHL, VHL, NPHL, BMHL and MBHL).
- [InvIT platform] Shrem InvIT holds projects located in Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Uttar Pradesh, Gujarat and Karnataka; upcoming assets earmarked for InvIT transfer span roads, transmission, renewable and oil and gas.
- [Order book contradiction] The Company Overview slide states a 'Rs 30,215 Cr Diversified Order Book across 12 verticals', while the order book slide states 'Order Book as at 30th June 2026 of Rs. 27,691 Cr' with a footnote that it 'Excludes: New Irrigation Project won in July 2026 in the state of Chhattisgarh, with a total project cost of Rs. 2,524.32 Cr' — both readings are quoted here without reconciliation.
- [Mining order book treatment] The company holds long-term order book from its Mining MDOs for the next 25-55 years but has included only 3 years of rolling orders worth Rs 5,224 Cr in the reported order book (Rs 2,247 Cr from DBL Siarmal Coal Mines, Rs 1,374 Cr from Pachhwara Coal Mine and Rs 1,603 Cr from DBL Pottangi Bauxite Mines).
- [Leadership] Dilip Suryavanshi is Chairman and Managing Director (43+ years in construction, President of the Madhya Pradesh Builders Association) and Devendra Jain is Managing Director and CEO (26+ years); the senior team includes Rohan Suryavanshi (Head – Strategy & Planning), Karan Suryavanshi (Head – Business Development), Bharat Singh (President) and Sanjay Bansal (CFO, joined 2022).

themes.title: Infrastructure EPC & roads order-book conversion
themes.need: India's record capital-outlay cycle (roads, metro, marine, hydro, tunnelling) gives diversified EPC contractors multi-year visibility - AFCONS tracks a ~INR4 lakh cr pipeline (70% domestic) and targets ~INR30,000cr FY27 inflow; NCC/DBL/PNCINFRA/GRINFRA/ASHOKA/CEIGALL carry large road/HAM books; AFCONS/PATELENG/AHLUCONT/PSPPROJECT add marine, hydro and building EPC. The binding issue is execution + client-payment cycles, not order intake.
themes.driver: L1-to-firm-order conversion (AFCONS Croatia/Vadhavan, DMRC awards); NHAI/HAM award pickup; monsoon-end execution ramp.

hero.oneLiner: Dilip Buildcon is a pan-India diversified infrastructure company that has grown over 35+ years from a road-focused EPC contractor into a three-engine platform combining EPC execution, long-tenure coal and bauxite mine development and operation, and an InvIT-based asset-monetisation business.
